diagram_math_checks.result: Read def-monoidal-category and def-canonical-morphism-between-parenthesised-words locally. The associator is alpha(X,Y,Z):((X tensor Y) tensor Z) -> X tensor(Y tensor Z). This is an arbitrary monoidal category, with no coefficient field/ring or linearity convention required. Identities 1_A and 1_D are morphisms; tensoring them is the given bifunctor. All parentheses are retained; no strictness, suppressed associators, inverses or scalar coefficients are assumed.

s=((A tensor B) tensor C) tensor D; m=(A tensor B) tensor(C tensor D); t=A tensor(B tensor(C tensor D)); u=(A tensor(B tensor C)) tensor D; v=A tensor((B tensor C) tensor D). These are precisely the five binary parenthesisations of the ordered four letters A,B,C,D, evaluated in the same category.

s -> m is alpha(A tensor B,C,D), by substituting X=A tensor B,Y=C,Z=D in the local associator type. m -> t is alpha(A,B,C tensor D). The resulting composite alpha(A,B,C tensor D) after alpha(A tensor B,C,D) is exactly step 1.1.

s -> u is alpha(A,B,C) tensor 1_D; u -> v is alpha(A,B tensor C,D); v -> t is 1_A tensor alpha(B,C,D). Each target equals the next source with its full parentheses. Their right-to-left composition is exactly step 1.2.

The sole asserted relation is equality of the upper two-arrow and lower three-arrow composites s -> t. Verification step 2.1 obtains it from L1 (thm-mac-lane-coherence-in-the-canonical-map-form): all five arrows and both composites are canonical, with common source and target. The same equality matches the local monoidal-category pentagon axiom with W=A,X=B,Y=C,Z=D. No additional diagonal, equality of differently parenthesised objects, or unit relation is asserted. The original rigorous proof is unchanged and remains independent of the figure.
